reviews.t: R-NEU 400 Cotton Rounds, 100% Natural Turkish Cotton Makeup Remover and Facial Cleansing Cotto
reviews.x: These cotton pads are too thin to be very absorbent.  There are plenty of rounds for the money.  But I find myself using 2 at a time to assist with extra absorbency when needed.  For my intended usage from makeup removal to nail polish removal, I find that I need a thicker pad. Pros: Lots of pads for your $. Do not release linty bits. Cons:  Too thin for my usage.

I use these to apply toner to my face 2x per day. I don't need rounds that are ultra thick or soft, since I only use them for a couple seconds a day. These work perfectly.  I don't know if these would hold up well for something like removing nail polish.  But for a quick swipe of toner, these are the most affordable option I've found.

Swisspers is my usual brand but for some strange reason I decided to give these a try. They're "ok" ...they are soft and absorbent but they tend to shed fibers even when wet. As I use these around my eye area that is not a good thing! Will return to my usual rounds.

reviews.t: These are great and better than expected
reviews.x: These rounds are nicely made. They’re soft, absorbent, and really do not shed. I’m a guy, so it’s especially nice the cotton doesn’t leave lint or fuzzies on my face stubble. These are great for cleaning the face, even cleaning little household items, and for applying nail polish remover. These hold their round shape and don’t fall apart, and the tiny ridges on one side are helpful if you need a little texture.
I was concerned that they were so thin but they turned out to be quite strong. Did not fall apart when using with facial cleanser. Absorbent too.
These are convenient, but thinner than expected. Seems about half as thin as other cotton round pads I would buy at the store.
Exactly what I expected. Really like the product.

reviews.t: Lint free?! Don't you believe it!
reviews.x: NOT lint free, that's for sure! As soon as I opened the package and grabbed the first pad, lint fell like snow! The pads are cut with a stamp and that's the lint part; bits and pieces of cut pads. But the pad itself when you use it (I use them with witch hazel) is lint free for the most part. The only thing left behind on my face are those bits and pieces from the cutting of the pads. Other than that, they seem to fit the bill and I'm not going to return them. This is one of those amazing buys where you’re stocked for the next 6 months and at first glance you think they’re going to be really thin but they’re not at all I was actually super surprised and there good quality too better than what I normally buy and I wasn’t expecting each leave to come in their own resealable bag which is great keeps it clean so as long as they continue to offer this product  I’ll continue to buy it

reviews.t: You get what you pay for
reviews.x: I thought getting the cheaper ones would be fine. And they are FINE I mean they work... but it's clear they're cheap. Every single one has scraps from when they were punched out during manufacturing. The edges are almost sharp, and the little flakes have gotten in my eyes. I have to pick them off before I use the pads. Just not ideal but not something I feel comfortable just throwing away.

claims.text: Many reviewers find these cotton rounds soft, absorbent, and good value, often comparing them favorably to store brands.
A common complaint is that the rounds are thin and flimsy, with some saying they fall apart or shed cotton during use.
Several reviewers report the product received did not match the description or previous orders, calling it false advertising.
Some reviewers note the rounds lack a quilted or textured side and have holes or perforations that reduce effectiveness.
Some reviewers with sensitive skin found the rounds scratchy, while others reported no shredding and that they hold their shape.

qa.q: Are these cotton rounds soft enough for sensitive skin?
qa.answer: Reviews disagree on softness for sensitive skin: one reviewer found them scratchy on sensitive skin [1], while others describe them as soft [2][3]. One reviewer also notes that being so soft is not a good thing for removing embedded makeup [5].

claims.text: One reviewer found them wafer thin and scratchy on sensitive skin [1].
Other reviewers describe the rounds as soft [2][3].
One reviewer says being so soft is not a good thing for removing embedded anything without a quilted side [5].

qa.q: Do they shed lint or leave fibers on my face?
qa.answer: Reviews disagree: some report shedding fibers or cotton bits on the face [1][3][5], while others say they do not shed or leave lint [4][6].

claims.text: Some reviews report lint, cotton shavings, or fibers left on the face.
Other reviews say the rounds do not shed or leave lint or fuzzies on the face.

qa.q: How well do they hold up when wet—do they fall apart?
qa.answer: Reviews disagree on wet durability: one reviewer says they did not fall apart when used with facial cleanser [4], while another reports they shed fibers even when wet [2].

claims.text: They did not fall apart when using with facial cleanser.
They tend to shed fibers even when wet.

qa.q: Are they thick enough to use with toner or makeup remover?
qa.answer: Reviews disagree on thickness: some say they are thin but work well for toner [1][2][3], while others find them too thin for makeup removal and needing multiple pads [5][6]. One reviewer specifically notes the lack of a quilted side makes them less effective for removing makeup with toner [4].

claims.text: These are thin but work perfectly for applying toner [1][2].
They are thin but strong and did not fall apart with facial cleanser [3].
Some find them wafer thin and use 2 or 3 at a time [5].
They are too thin to be very absorbent and a thicker pad is needed for makeup removal [6].
The lack of a quilted side makes them less effective for removing makeup with toner [4].

qa.q: Do they have any smell or chemical odor out of the pack?
qa.answer: Not enough evidence in reviews to answer this.
